form_basis: prohibited practice: "or is a medium" (18:11)
note: The negation sits in 18:10, whose list of forbidden practices this verse continues.

form_basis: prohibited practice: "or observes portents" (18:11)
note: The negation sits in 18:10, whose list this verse continues. Seed N9 names the Hebrew yidoni; the Saints Translation reads 'observes portents'.

form_basis: prohibited practice: "or inquires of the dead" (18:11)
note: The negation sits in 18:10, whose list of forbidden practices this verse continues.

form_basis: "you shall hearken unto him" (18:15)
note: Heeding God's prophet is obedience to God (Moral), not a rite; 'Fulfilled' reflects Christ as the promised prophet (Acts 3:22), not ceremonial character.

form_basis: court penalty: "that prophet shall die" (18:20)
note: Seeds N26/N27 are the bans implied by the offence; the verse states only the penalty ('that prophet shall die'), a court duty, so Positive.

form_basis: "you shall not spare him" (18:22)
"you shall add three cities more" (19:9)
"Your eye shall not spare him" (19:13)
note: Mixed: also 'you shall cleanse the guilt of innocent blood from Israel' (19:13), the positive aim of carrying out the judgment.

form_basis: "You shall not remove your neighbour’s boundaries" (19:14)
note: The brief lists boundaries as Civil; moving a neighbour's marker is also theft, hence Moral secondary.

form_basis: "two witnesses ... shall every matter be established" (19:15)
note: Mixed: also 'One witness shall not suffice' (N288); the title leads with the two-witness rule. Court procedure (Civil); 'Unchanged' reflects NT reuse (John 8:17).

form_basis: court penalty: "do unto him as he wickedly purposed" (19:19)
note: Mixed: also 'Your eye shall not spare him' (19:21), forbidding leniency in applying the penalty.

form_basis: "you shall not fear them" (20:1)
note: War provision, Civil under the brief's tie-breaker; it is not a rite of worship, so it departs from the Covenant-specific (Ceremonial) pairing.

form_basis: "the scribes shall speak unto the people" (20:5)
note: The scribes must announce the exemptions; for the exempted man 'Let him go' works as a permission, but the record frames the duty to honour them.

form_basis: "call ... forth with an offer of peace" (20:10)
status: "shall pay you tribute, and be subject" (20:11)
"you shall slay every male therein" (20:13)
exception: "save the women and the dependent households" (20:14)
note: 'Save' marks an exception to the slaying command; read as a required protected status for women and households, so Positive rather than Negative or Permission.

form_basis: "you shall take as spoil unto yourself" (20:14)
note: 'Take as spoil unto yourself' grants rather than requires, as the context note says. War law, so Civil rather than the Covenant-specific (Ceremonial) pairing.

form_basis: "you shall utterly devote them to destruction" (20:17)
note: N49 (save none alive) rests on 20:16, outside this text, so not mixed. Conquest command (Civil); 'utterly devote' (herem) adds a devoted-things character.

form_basis: "you shall not destroy its trees" (20:19)
note: 20:20 adds permissions ('you may destroy' trees bearing no fruit); permissions are not requirements, so not mixed.

form_basis: "you shall send her forth free" (21:14)
note: The verse's other clauses (no sale, no contempt) are separate records C1114 and C1115, so not mixed.

form_basis: "she shall not be sold for silver" (21:14)
note: Selling her would treat a freed woman as property, a wrong in itself, hence Moral secondary.

form_basis: "You shall not treat her with contempt" (21:14)
note: Mistreatment ban within the captive-marriage law (Civil); its moral ground could make it Moral. Seed N264 reads the Hebrew as enslaving her.

form_basis: "he may not make ... the firstborn" (21:16)
"he shall acknowledge the firstborn" (21:17)
court penalty: "the men of his city shall stone him" (21:21)
"you shall surely bury him that day" (21:23)
note: Mixed: also 'his body shall not remain upon the tree overnight' (N66). Execution procedure (Civil); 'you shall not defile the land' adds a purity character.

form_basis: "you shall surely bring them back" (22:1)
note: Mixed: also 'You shall not see ... and disregard them' (22:1) and 'you may not disregard it' (22:3), per N269.

form_basis: "you shall gather them into your house" (22:2)
"A woman shall not have a man’s equipment" (22:5)
note: 'Abomination' and the distinction of the sexes suggest Moral (traditionally under the seventh commandment); some read it as a pagan-cult or separation rule (Ceremonial).

form_basis: "neither shall a man put on" (22:5)
note: 'Abomination' and the distinction of the sexes suggest Moral (traditionally under the seventh commandment); some read it as a pagan-cult or separation rule (Ceremonial).

form_basis: "You shall surely let the mother go" (22:7)
note: Mixed: also 'you shall not take the mother with the young' (22:6); 22:7 permits taking the young. Treated as land-use law; compassion or food-law readings possible.

form_basis: "you shall make a parapet for your roof" (22:8)
note: Mixed: also 'that you do not cause bloodshed in your house' (N298), a purpose clause read as a ban on leaving hazards. Protecting life gives Moral secondary.

form_basis: "You shall not sow your vineyard" (22:9)
status rule: "become consecrated" (22:9)
note: Status rule: the yield 'become[s] consecrated' (forfeit). Seed N216 reads this as a ban on benefit; the record states the status itself, so Positive.

form_basis: "You shall not plough" (22:10)
note: Mixed yoking is a separation law, which the brief places under Ceremonial, so this departs from the site's civil label.

form_basis: court penalty: "shall take that man and chasten him" (22:18)
court penalty: "they shall fine him a hundred shekels" (22:19)
"he may not put her away" (22:19)
note: Mixed: also 'she shall be his wife' (P219), the duty to keep her as wife.

form_basis: court penalty: "the men of her city shall stone her" (22:21)
court penalty: "they shall be stoned with stones" (22:24)
court penalty: "you shall put to death only the man" (22:25)
"unto the young woman you shall do nothing" (22:26)
note: Not punishing the coerced victim is a court rule (Civil) resting on justice to the innocent, hence Moral secondary.

form_basis: penalty payment: "shall give unto the father ... fifty silver didrachmas" (22:29)
"she shall be his wife" (22:29)
note: Marriage obligation imposed as a consequence of the violation (Civil), with Moral secondary as the underlying act is a sexual wrong.

form_basis: "he may not put her away" (22:29)
"shall not enter the assembly of the Lord" (23:2)
note: Treated as access to Israel's worshipping assembly; seed N360 reads 'enter the assembly' as marrying into Israel, which would be Civil.

form_basis: "shall not enter the assembly of the Lord" (23:3)
note: Treated as access to Israel's worshipping assembly; seed N354 (mamzer) reads it as a marriage ban. The Saints Translation reads 'One born of a prostitute'.

form_basis: "shall not enter the assembly of the Lord" (23:4)
note: Treated as access to Israel's worshipping assembly; seed N53 reads it as a marriage ban, and the national exclusion could also read as Civil.

form_basis: "You shall not speak peace unto them" (23:7)
note: National policy toward Ammon and Moab (war and government), so Civil.

form_basis: "You shall not abhor an Edomite" (23:8)
note: Forbids abhorring a brother nation (Moral), departing from the civil label; in context (23:9) and per seed N54 it also governs assembly admission.

form_basis: "you shall not abhor an Egyptian" (23:8)
note: Forbids abhorring the nation that hosted Israel (Moral), departing from the civil label; in context (23:9) and per seed N55 it also governs assembly admission.

form_basis: status: "shall enter the assembly of the Lord" (23:9)
note: Status rule ('shall enter'): Israel must admit the third generation; seeds N54–55 phrase it as not rejecting them. Assembly access is a worship matter, not civil.

form_basis: "you shall keep yourself from every evil thing" (23:10)
note: Heads the camp rules (23:10–15): war-camp discipline (Civil) with a camp-holiness character. Phrased positively ('keep yourself'), though in substance it bars every evil thing.

form_basis: "he shall go forth outside the camp" (23:11)
note: Mixed: also 'shall not enter the camp' (N78). The title leads with leaving and washing, so Positive; the brief counts impurity rules as positive.

form_basis: "you shall have a place outside the camp" (23:13)
note: Camp hygiene, which the brief lists as Civil; the passage's holiness motive (23:15) lies outside this verse.

form_basis: "You shall not deliver unto his master" (23:16)
note: Asylum rule for escaped slaves (Civil); shielding the fugitive from his master is also mercy to the oppressed, hence Moral secondary.

form_basis: status: "He shall dwell with you" (23:17)
note: Grants the escapee free residence; read as Israel's duty to allow it ('He shall dwell with you'), so Positive rather than Permission.

form_basis: "You shall not afflict him" (23:17)
note: Part of the escaped-slave asylum law (Civil); oppressing a vulnerable stranger is also a moral wrong (cf. Exod 22:21), which could make Moral primary.

form_basis: "There shall be no prostitute" (23:18)
"no woman who performs initiation rites" (23:18)
note: Bans pagan cult initiation, an idolatry prohibition (Moral), not a rite of Israel's worship; so it departs from the Covenant-specific (Ceremonial) pairing.

form_basis: "shall not bring the hire of a prostitute" (23:19)
"not bring ... nor the price of a dog" (23:19)
"Unto a foreigner you may lend at interest" (23:21)
note: Seed P198 reads a duty, but 'you may lend at interest' only permits, as the context note says; the brother clause is a separate prohibition.

form_basis: "you shall not delay to pay it" (23:22)
note: Vow law (Ceremonial); keeping one's word to God also has a moral core (cf. Eccl 5:4–5), hence Moral secondary.

form_basis: "you may gather heads of grain" (23:25)
note: Permission ('you may gather') limited by 'you shall not put a sickle' (a ban, not a requirement, so not mixed). Seeds P201/N267 apply it to hired workers.

form_basis: "you may eat grapes" (23:26)
note: Permission ('you may eat grapes') limited by 'you shall put none in a vessel' (a ban, not a requirement, so not mixed). Seeds P201/N268 apply it to hired workers.

form_basis: "former husband ... may not take her again" (24:4)
note: Operative clause is the remarriage ban (N356); P213/P222 rest on the case's conditions (24:1–3). Divorce law (Civil) with a sexual-purity character ('abomination', 'defiled').

form_basis: "he shall not go forth unto war" (24:5)
note: The title says 'exempt', but the verse's operative words forbid sending him to war or laying duty on him (N311), so Negative.

form_basis: "shall gladden his wife whom he has taken" (24:5)
note: The year at home is a civil exemption (Civil); its stated purpose, gladdening his wife, is a duty of marital love (Moral secondary).

form_basis: "You shall not take a mill ... in pledge" (24:6)
note: Pledge law (Civil); 'takes a life in pledge' grounds it in mercy to the debtor, hence Moral secondary.

form_basis: "you shall not enter his house" (24:10)
"same day you shall pay his wages" (24:15)
note: Mixed: also 'You shall not withhold the wages' (24:14). Withholding a poor man's pay is oppression (Moral); the same-day deadline is the civil detail.

form_basis: "Fathers shall not die for children" (24:16)
note: Seed N287 is the rabbinic reading (no testimony from relatives); the plain verse bars executing one person for another's sin. Same negative form.

form_basis: "neither shall you take a widow’s garment" (24:17)
note: Pledge law (Civil) protecting the widow, whose care is a moral duty, hence Moral secondary.

form_basis: "You shall not pervert the judgment" (24:17)
note: Justice for the vulnerable as a duty (Moral; cf. Deut 27:19); it concerns judgment in court, hence Civil secondary.

form_basis: "you shall not return to take it" (24:19)
note: Mixed: also 'It shall be for the poor...' (P122), assigning the forgotten sheaf to the poor.

form_basis: "you shall not return to glean what remains" (24:20)
note: Mixed: also 'It shall be for the sojourner...', assigning what remains to the poor.

form_basis: court penalty: "they shall scourge him before them" (25:2)
note: Mixed: also 'shall not add thereto' (25:3; N300), the forty-stripe limit.

form_basis: "You shall not muzzle an ox" (25:4)
note: Agricultural rule for Israel (Civil); the NT applies its principle to workers' pay (1 Cor 9:9), the moral character behind the 'Unchanged' label.

form_basis: "shall not be married outside unto a man" (25:5)
"Her husband’s brother shall go in unto her" (25:5)
status rule: "established in the name of the dead" (25:6)
status rule: "his name shall be called in Israel" (25:10)
note: Public designation imposed after the levirate refusal; a status consequence, so Positive.

form_basis: court penalty: "you shall cut off her hand" (25:12)
note: Mixed: also 'your eye shall not spare her' (N293). P247 (rescuing the pursued) is the rabbinic reading; the verse states a penalty.

form_basis: "You shall not have ... differing weights" (25:13)
curse: "Cursed is he who takes a bribe" (27:25)
note: Curse formula read as a prohibition; the people's 'So be it' is the covenant-ceremony response, not a separate standing provision.
